title: A small and short-lived rising at Pamplona, in the Ṭāʾifa of Banbalūna, gives the Emperor the occasion he wants

The Emperor calls a Jamāʿa and, in the pomp of victory, takes from the umarāʾ the right to raise and manage the empire's mercenaries, with several smaller reforms against their power. To win their votes he offers dozens of noble families land in the north, or claims on lands still held by Qashtāla for after the next war. The grants make them landlords, not lords: the conquests remain the property of the crown and the house of Naṣr
